scenarios.name: healthy
scenarios.title: A quiet network
scenarios.description: Nothing wrong. This is what the agent looks like when it has nothing to say, which is most of the time and is the hardest case to get right.

scenarios.name: evening_congestion
scenarios.title: Evening congestion
scenarios.description: Everything slows by about 45 percent at peak hours and nothing breaks. A detector that flags this is one you uninstall within a week.

scenarios.name: wifi_fade
scenarios.title: Walking away from the access point
scenarios.description: Signal fades, retries climb, the link rate collapses. The classic cause of a call breaking up, and the one users most often misdiagnose.

scenarios.name: wifi_interference
scenarios.title: A crowded Wi-Fi channel
scenarios.description: Signal strength stays fine but a third of frames need retransmitting. Distance is not the problem here, and the advice differs accordingly.

scenarios.name: dns_slow
scenarios.title: A slow resolver
scenarios.description: Name lookups climb from 20 ms to several hundred. Pages feel slow to start even though they transfer normally once open.

scenarios.name: dns_blackhole
scenarios.title: DNS stops answering
scenarios.description: Total resolver failure. Everything downstream fails too, so the interesting question is whether the agent blames the cause or a symptom.

scenarios.name: gateway_congestion
scenarios.title: The router is struggling
scenarios.description: Round trips to your own router rise from 3 ms to tens of milliseconds with heavy jitter. The problem is inside the building.

scenarios.name: gateway_down
scenarios.title: The router stops responding
scenarios.description: Nothing past it can be reached or measured. The agent has to say so without inventing conclusions about layers it can no longer see.

scenarios.name: isp_path_congestion
scenarios.title: Congestion past the router
scenarios.description: The local network stays clean; latency appears beyond the second hop. This is the case a single-layer tool always gets wrong.

scenarios.name: remote_service_slow
scenarios.title: The far end is slow
scenarios.description: DNS, the router and the path are all healthy. Only the service being contacted is slow, so the answer is that nothing is wrong with your network.

scenarios.name: tls_handshake_slow
scenarios.title: Slow TLS handshakes
scenarios.description: The encrypted setup at the start of each connection dominates. Phase timing is the only way to see this at all.

scenarios.name: vpn_overload
scenarios.title: A saturated VPN tunnel
scenarios.description: Extra latency appears inside the tunnel rather than on the path to it, and retransmissions rise with it.

scenarios.name: device_pressure
scenarios.title: The laptop itself is the bottleneck
scenarios.description: CPU is pinned and the network stack is starved. The network is fine; the machine is not.

scenarios.name: captive_portal
scenarios.title: A hotel sign-in page
scenarios.description: Something intercepts every request at once. Every layer looks broken, and blaming the internet provider would be confidently wrong.

stats.source: netpulse eval, the same figures CI gates on
